items.prompt: Xi jkun hemm il-Ħadd filgħaxija?
Write on 10 February in Maltese, with the number in words.
Write on 19 March in Maltese, with the number in words.
Make the whole sentence plural, with boys and green marbles: It-tifel sab boċċa ħadra.
items.hint: Check both noun groups. The verb follows the boys, and the adjective follows the marbles.
items.explanation: Subien means boys, so the verb changes from sab to sabu. Boċċi and boċoċ are both plural forms of boċċa, and ħodor agrees with either plural.

items.prompt: You are speaking to two friends. Rewrite the whole command for both of them: Agħlaq it-tieqa.
items.hint: The listeners change in number. The window is still singular.
items.explanation: Agħlaq addresses one person. Agħlqu addresses more than one, and the initial i of it-tieqa drops after the vowel u.

items.prompt: Rewrite the whole sentence about yourself, beginning with Jien or Jiena: Rita taħsel il-platti u tara ftit televiżjoni.
items.answer: Jien naħsel il-platti u nara ftit televiżjoni
items.answerTranslation: I wash the dishes and watch a little television.
accepted: Jien naħsel il-platti u nara ftit televiżjoni
Jiena naħsel il-platti u nara ftit televiżjoni
items.hint: Look for the subject change in both verbs.
items.explanation: Taħsel and tara describe what Rita does. Both verbs take n- with jien or jiena: naħsel and nara.

items.prompt: Answer in one Maltese sentence beginning with Il-festa ta' San Pawl and using issir. Meta ssir il-festa ta' San Pawl? Write the date 10 February entirely in words.
items.answer: Il-festa ta' San Pawl issir fl-għaxra ta' Frar
items.answerTranslation: The feast of St Paul takes place on 10 February.
items.hint: Write the date as a phrase starting with fl-.
items.explanation: Use issir with the feminine subject il-festa. In this date, fl-għaxra ta' Frar means on the tenth of February.

items.prompt: Rewrite the whole sentence about a female cat: Il-qattus kien mxarrab wara x-xita.
items.answerTranslation: The female cat was wet after the rain.
items.hint: Check the noun, the verb and the adjective for feminine agreement.
items.explanation: Qattusa is feminine, so kien becomes kienet and mxarrab becomes mxarrba. Wara x-xita (after the rain) stays the same.

items.prompt: Make the whole sentence plural, with several mice and several holes: Il-ġurdien ħareġ mit-toqba.
items.answerTranslation: The mice came out of the holes.
items.hint: Both nouns change internally. Match the verb to the mice.
items.explanation: Ġrieden and toqob are broken plurals. The plural subject takes ħarġu. Mit- still means out of the and attaches to toqob.

items.prompt: Tell one person in one Maltese sentence: Turn left and keep going straight to the square. Use dur and ibqa' sejjer, in that order.
items.answer: Dur fuq ix-xellug u ibqa' sejjer dritt sal-pjazza
items.answerTranslation: Turn left and keep going straight to the square.
items.hint: Give the turn first. Then use dritt and an endpoint with sa.
items.explanation: Fuq ix-xellug gives the turn direction. Sal-pjazza means as far as the square, which marks the endpoint of ibqa' sejjer dritt.

items.prompt: Rewrite the whole sentence about us, beginning with Aħna: Jien nixtri ftit frott.
items.hint: The first-person prefix stays. Check the verb ending.
items.explanation: With aħna, nixtri becomes nixtru. The n- prefix stays, and the ending -u marks the plural subject. Ftit frott means some fruit.

items.prompt: Give one person a recipe instruction in one Maltese sentence: Add a little hot water and stir. Use żid and ħawwad.
items.answer: Żid ftit ilma jaħraq u ħawwad
items.answerTranslation: Add a little hot water and stir.
items.hint: Put the amount before the water and the adjective after it.
items.explanation: Use żid and ħawwad as commands to one person. Jaħraq describes the water and comes after ilma. Ftit indicates a small amount.

items.prompt: Rewrite the whole sentence about your sister, using the feminine equivalent of huwa: Ħija huwa twil.
items.hint: Change the family word as well as the pronoun and the adjective.
items.explanation: Oħti means my sister, while ħija means my brother. Hija and twila agree with the feminine subject.

items.prompt: Make the gardens and the broken benches plural in this sentence: Fil-ġnien kien hemm bank imkisser.
items.answerTranslation: There were broken benches in the gardens.
items.hint: Choose the plural of bank that refers to a seat. Keep the expression for there were.
items.explanation: Ġonna is the plural of ġnien. Use bankijiet for benches and imkissrin to describe them. Kien hemm is the same in this expression for there was or there were.

items.prompt: Answer from Il-Festi in one Maltese sentence. Start with Il-Ħadd filgħaxija and use toħroġ. Xi jkun hemm il-Ħadd filgħaxija? Include what is carried.
items.answerTranslation: On Sunday evening, the procession sets out with the statue.
items.explanation: The procession takes place on Sunday evening. Toħroġ agrees with il-purċissjoni, and bil-vara specifies that the statue is carried.
